ctx: John 5 begins with a healing on the Sabbath and the anger it provokes. From verse 19 Jesus explains his work and his claims. Verses 31 to 47 are his case: the evidence for what he has said.
This is the rule of Study 2 from the other side. In chapter 8 the second witness was the Father. In chapter 5 he lines up the whole bench.
inv: He starts by granting the rule, in terms that sound like self-defeat:

inv.q: If I testify concerning Myself, My testimony is not true

inv: . This is the law of witness stated against himself, on purpose. He will not ask for belief on his own word. He will call others.
Count them. First, John the Baptist:

inv.q: he has testified to the truth
the same works that I do, testify concerning Me
the Father Himself, has testified concerning Me
these are they testifying concerning Me

inv: . Five voices of five different kinds: a man, a deed, God, a book, and the lawgiver.
The fourth and fifth witnesses are the reason this series reads the Old Testament as testimony. His opponents searched the Scriptures carefully,

inv.q: because you think to have eternal life in them
are not willing to come to Me

inv: . They held the witness in their hands and would not hear what it said. Reading the text was not their failure. Reading it as an end, and not as testimony that points beyond itself, was.
Then Moses stops being a distant authority and becomes a witness in court:

inv.q: There is the one accusing you: Moses, in whom you have hoped
But if you do not believe his writings, how will you believe My words?

inv: Christ's authority is argued from the Old Testament's, not set against it.

w: Study 2: the two-witness rule in chapter 8, with the Father as the second witness.
x.q: the testimony of two men is true

w: After the resurrection Christ does what he does here: he reads the Old Testament as testimony about himself.
x.q: He interpreted to them the things concerning Himself in all the Scriptures

w: He names the three divisions of the Old Testament that bear witness.
x.q: all things having been written concerning Me in the Law of Moses and the Prophets and the Psalms

w: One place where Moses writes of a prophet like himself whom the people are told to hear.
x.q: The Lord thy God shall raise up to thee a prophet of thy brethren, like me; him shall ye hear

take: Christ calls five witnesses and the Old Testament is among them. To hold Moses and the Prophets in your hands and refuse to hear what they say of him is the failure he names here.
